taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes a proposed move to Hesperosciurus, tentatively not accepted per the American Society of Mammalogists (2024).
fieldMarks: Silver-gray back with a white underside
Long bushy silver-gray tail, may contain black
behavior: Active year round; may stay in the nest in severe weather
Most active early morning and late afternoon
Eats acorns, nuts, conifer seeds, fungi, berries, green vegetation and insects; buries acorns
habitat: Fairly open oak and pine-oak forest, also riparian woods and lowland walnut groves; nests in tree cavities or on limbs.
range: Lake Chelan and Tacoma, Washington south through Oregon, western Nevada, and the Sierra Nevada and coast ranges of California to Baja California.
